name: Unboxing Video
summary: A fixed top-down shot of a table. Two hands open a box and lift out a product, and a voice names each part. The look is plain on purpose, so the object is the star.

philosophy.core_thesis: The viewer owns the first touch by proxy: show the opening of the box in real time and let the object, not the frame, carry the interest.
design_principles: Fix the camera above the table at 90° and frame the box at 40% to 60% of the picture height.
Use a plain ground in light grey or white (#F2EFE9) with no pattern and no props.
Show only two hands, with no face, until the product is out of the box.
Keep each cut at 4s to 12s; hold a close-up of the product for at least 3s.
Name each part with a lower-third label of 24px to 32px for 2s at the moment the part appears.
Show the price or the model name in one chip in the top-right corner for the full clip.
Light the table from the front at 5600K so that shadows stay soft and the colours stay true.
anti_patterns: Dark, moody grounds with heavy vignettes
Quick cuts under 2s that hide the object
Busy desk props around the box
Dense on-screen text over the product

layout.grid_mechanics: A 16:9 frame with a centre stage of 60% width. Lower-third labels sit on a 12-column grid with 24px gutters.
layout.whitespace_ratio: 35% to 50% of the frame is empty table; the spacing scale is 8, 16, 24 and 48px.
layout.alignment_rules: The product stays centred; labels align flush-left at 48px from the frame edge; the price chip aligns top-right.
layout.container_geometry: Chips and labels with an 8px radius and a 2px edge; the box and the product stay as real objects with true edges.

font_pairings.note: A friendly, rounded sans for labels with a neutral text face.
A heavy label face for the model name with a plain body face.
A clean geometric display face for chips and lower-thirds.

typography.tracking: Display takes 0em; labels take +0.04em in capitals.
hierarchy_rules: Use two weights: medium (500) and bold (700).
Set the model name in bold at 56px and each part label at 24px.
Set the price chip in capitals at 14px.

color.palette_structure: A neutral table with white and cardboard, one orange label colour and one blue tape accent.
color.contrast_rules: Text on the table grey holds at least 14:1; orange carries chips and rules, not body text.
color.surface_treatment: Flat, matte table colour with a soft, 2% grain; no gradient on the ground.
color.light_and_shadow: Soft front light; a 16px blur shadow at 14% black under each object.

materiality.surface_simulation: A real desk, a cardboard box, shrink film and moulded foam shown as shot, with true material colour.
materiality.border_rules: A 2px solid edge in black at 12% on chips; no edge on the table.
materiality.blur_and_elevation: A 16px soft shadow under the box and the labels; no backdrop blur.

ornamentation_details.iconography: Outline icons at 24px with a 2px stroke for storage, weight and size; round terminals.
ornamentation_details.illustration: No illustration; the real object and the real box are the only picture.

motion.transition_physics: Labels slide in 24px from the left over 200ms and hold for 2s; the cut between parts is a hard cut with no wipe.
motion.hover_and_active: Hover raises a chip by 2px and adds a 16px shadow; active state darkens the fill by 8%.

emotion.target_response: The viewer feels curious and impatient, as if the box were in their own hands.

avoid_when: The product has no physical form.
The brand needs a cinematic or luxury mood.
The page needs dense data instead of one object.

modifiers.how: Add a shocked face, a red arrow and a 120px headline; keep the product at the centre.
Move the mic close, slow every action to 2x length and remove all labels.
Add a face window of 20% width in the lower-right corner and talk over the product.

pack.why: A plain outline family with round terminals fits the neutral labels and chips of a product shot.

ground.why: The ground is the plain, pale table that every unboxing shot starts from.
